paragraphs: GeCo tackles counting objects in images when only a few annotated examples, or none, are available. Existing counters build appearance prototypes and search for matching objects. When objects look different from one another, these prototypes can become too broad and match things that should not count. GeCo combines object detection, segmentation, and counting in one architecture to address this problem.

Its first change is a dense object query formulation that helps prototypes generalize across differences in object appearance. Its second change concerns training. Common methods ask the model to predict a Gaussian-shaped target around each annotated object center. That indirect objective is sensitive to annotation errors and hyperparameter choices. GeCo instead introduces a counting loss that directly optimizes detection.

The authors report approximately 25% lower total-count mean absolute error than leading detection-based few-shot counters, alongside better detection accuracy. They also report state-of-the-art results across the low-shot counting setups studied. These findings support treating accurate object localization and counting as closely connected tasks, with the training objective explicitly reflecting the detections needed for a correct count.
neurips-2024-a-novel-unified-architectur.tldr: GeCo unifies detection, segmentation, and low-shot counting, improving counts through appearance-aware object queries and a detection-focused training loss.

paragraphs: cPAPERS addresses conversations about scientific papers in which a question depends on a particular equation, figure, table, or passage. Such interactions require more than understanding the paper as a block of text: a useful response must connect the question to the relevant component and its context. The dataset is designed around this grounded form of scientific discussion.

The authors collect conversational question-and-answer pairs from academic paper reviews on OpenReview. They associate those exchanges with contextual information extracted from the LaTeX source files of scientific documents available on arXiv. The resulting dataset links conversations to paper components and their associated references, bringing the discussion and the material it concerns into the same resource.

The work also presents baseline approaches using large language models, both without task-specific fine-tuning and after fine-tuning. These approaches provide starting points for studying how models handle the dataset. The contribution is a data collection strategy and a benchmark resource for component-grounded scientific conversations, together with initial modeling approaches for that setting.
neurips-2024-cpapers-a-dataset-of-situat.tldr: cPAPERS connects scientific review conversations to the text, equations, figures, tables, and references they discuss.

paragraphs: This paper studies models that learn from several modalities and must work on unfamiliar data distributions containing the same modalities. The authors identify two obstacles: modalities compete during learning, and their individual loss landscapes have different degrees of flatness. A technique that improves generalization for a single modality therefore offers only limited gains in this multimodal setting.

The proposed method optimizes the loss landscape over learned representations rather than model parameters. This makes it possible to connect modalities directly by mixing their representations. The method seeks to flatten high-loss regions between minima associated with different modalities, using interpolated representations to support knowledge transfer. It distills and optimizes these representations while assigning different weights to modalities according to their differing generalization capabilities.

Experiments on EPIC-Kitchens and Human-Animal-Cartoon cover multiple modality combinations and both single-source and multiple-source training. The reported results support the effectiveness of this representation-based approach in those settings. Its central contribution is to make cross-modal relationships part of the generalization objective, instead of relying only on flatness measures developed for individual modalities.
neurips-2024-cross-modal-representation-.tldr: The method improves multimodal generalization by flattening loss regions between modalities through mixed representations and cross-modal knowledge transfer.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning can make a foundation model better suited to a task while weakening its performance when the data distribution changes. Existing robustness methods often try to retain the model's pretrained features. This paper argues that preservation needs to be selective, because some pretrained features are themselves unreliable under distribution shifts.

Dual risk minimization, or DRM, combines a training-data performance objective with a worst-case risk objective. To estimate the latter, the method uses language-model-generated descriptions of the task's core features. Those descriptions induce zero-shot predictions based on the core features, which serve as proxies for estimating worst-case risk. The resulting objective balances expected performance with protection against poor performance under shifts.

The authors report state-of-the-art robustness across several real-world benchmarks. For CLIP ViT-L/14@336, the reported out-of-distribution scores rise from 75.9 to 77.1 on ImageNet, 47.1 to 51.8 on WILDS-iWildCam, and 50.7 to 53.1 on WILDS-FMoW. These findings support using task-relevant feature descriptions to guide what fine-tuning preserves, while the worst-case component remains based on the method's proxy estimates.
neurips-2024-dual-risk-minimization-towa.tldr: DRM uses language-generated core-feature descriptions to balance ordinary training performance with estimated worst-case risk during fine-tuning.

paragraphs: EGonc addresses graph node classification when some nodes may belong to categories absent from training. A model must classify familiar nodes while rejecting unfamiliar ones. Prediction confidence alone is problematic because neural networks can be highly confident about unseen data. The paper instead uses an energy-based model to estimate whether an input resembles the training distribution.

The method first generates substitute unknown examples using graph structure, aiming to mimic real open-set samples. It then learns an additional energy-based score for a virtual unknown class. This score comes from the part of a feature representation outside its principal space and is aligned with the original class scores through constant scaling. The virtual class score becomes the signal for detecting out-of-distribution nodes.

The authors establish theoretical properties guaranteeing an overall distinguishable margin between in-distribution and out-of-distribution detection scores. They also report superior performance in comprehensive experiments. The approach brings two ideas together: learning from constructed unknowns and explicitly representing unfamiliarity in the classification scores, rather than relying solely on confidence among known classes.
neurips-2024-egonc-energy-based-open-set.tldr: EGonc uses graph-informed substitute unknowns and an energy-based virtual class to detect unfamiliar nodes while classifying familiar ones.

paragraphs: FedMRL studies federated learning in which participating clients use models with different architectures. Existing approaches exchange knowledge through training losses, which the authors identify as a restriction on what clients and the server can share. FedMRL adds a small model with a common architecture alongside each client's distinct local model, creating a shared route for representation learning.

A lightweight, personalized projector fuses features from the shared and local models. This lets the fusion adapt to each client's data distribution while combining generalized and personalized information. The fused features then form Matryoshka representations: representations learned at multiple dimensions and levels of granularity through the shared and local prediction heads. These multiple perspectives are intended to improve learning beyond loss-based knowledge transfer.

The theoretical analysis gives a non-convex convergence rate of O(1/T). Benchmark experiments report better accuracy with low communication and computation costs compared with seven leading baselines. The reported gains reach up to 8.48% over the state of the art and 24.94% over the best same-category baseline; these are maximum reported improvements, not gains promised for every client or dataset.
neurips-2024-federated-model-heterogeneo.tldr: FedMRL helps federated clients with different model architectures share knowledge through personalized fusion and representations learned at multiple granularities.

paragraphs: FM-Delta targets the storage burden created by keeping many fine-tuned versions of large foundation models. Storing every version independently repeats much of the information already present in its pretrained parent. The authors' empirical and theoretical analysis finds that most fine-tuned models in the cloud differ only slightly from their pretrained versions, motivating compression based on those differences.

The method maps pretrained and fine-tuned parameter values into integers with the same bits, then entropy-codes the differences between those integers. A storage service retains one uncompressed pretrained model and compressed versions of its fine-tuned descendants. Because the scheme is lossless, its storage savings preserve the stored model parameters exactly rather than approximating them with reduced-precision values.

Experiments report average storage reductions of around 50%, with negligible added time in most end-to-end cases. For a collection of up to ten fine-tuned GPT-NeoX-20B models, storage falls from 423 GB to 205 GB. The findings show how shared ancestry among model variants can become a practical storage advantage when their parameter differences are encoded efficiently.
neurips-2024-fm-delta-lossless-compressi.tldr: FM-Delta losslessly compresses fine-tuned models relative to a shared pretrained model, reducing storage by around 50% on average in experiments.

paragraphs: PGT-Aug addresses class imbalance in LiDAR-based 3D object detection. Copying annotated objects from existing point clouds into new scenes can provide extra examples, but rare classes still have limited diversity, and suitable placement remains difficult. The proposed method expands the source of training objects to include low-cost miniatures and real-world videos.

Its pipeline first reconstructs volumetric 3D objects using a model that synthesizes views from 2D input. It then aligns the reconstructed objects with the LiDAR domain, including simulation of LiDAR intensity. Finally, it places objects using a context-aware method that combines ground and map information. These stages address object creation, sensor appearance, and scene placement as connected parts of augmentation.

The authors report detection improvements on nuScenes, KITTI, and Lyft, supporting the method's usefulness across the evaluated benchmarks. Improvements are especially emphasized for datasets separated by large domain gaps caused by different LiDAR configurations. The findings suggest that reconstructed pseudo-LiDAR objects can provide useful training variation when existing real point clouds offer too few diverse examples of minority classes.
neurips-2024-just-add-100-more-augmentin.tldr: PGT-Aug turns miniatures or videos into aligned, contextually placed pseudo-LiDAR objects to improve training for underrepresented classes.

paragraphs: This paper asks a basic theoretical question: can an agent learn to produce valid new strings from an unknown language without identifying the language itself? The setup gives the agent examples revealed by an adversary. The target language is known only to belong to a candidate list, which may be infinite.

Success is defined as generation in the limit. After some finite point in the sequence of revealed examples, the agent must produce strings that belong to the target language and have not yet appeared. The main result establishes that an agent with this property exists for every countable list of candidate languages. The guarantee concerns eventual generation after that finite point, rather than correctness from the first example.

This result contrasts with established impossibility results for identifying an unknown language from examples. The distinction matters because generation asks for valid unseen members, whereas identification asks which language is being observed. The paper shows that these goals have fundamentally different possibilities in its formal setting, providing a theoretical separation between learning to generate and learning to identify.
neurips-2024-language-generation-in-the-.tldr: For every countable candidate-language list, an agent can eventually generate valid unseen strings even though identifying the target language can be impossible.

paragraphs: Different neural models can organize information into different representation spaces, making it difficult to compare their internal features or transfer information between them. This paper approaches those spaces as low-dimensional manifolds and draws on spectral geometry to describe their relationships. Its central move is to work in the functional domain, providing another way to express alignment between spaces.

Latent Functional Maps is a framework with three related uses. It can compare representation spaces through interpretable measures of intrinsic similarity, find correspondences with either no supervision or weak supervision, and transfer representations between distinct spaces. Bringing these operations into one framework makes comparison and transfer parts of a shared geometric treatment rather than separate modeling problems.

The authors validate the framework across multiple modalities and applications, including stitching and retrieval tasks. They report reduced complexity, greater interpretability, and improved downstream performance from the functional approach. The stated findings support the framework's versatility across the tested uses, with its contribution centered on a common language for relating learned spaces.
neurips-2024-latent-functional-maps-a-sp.tldr: Latent Functional Maps uses spectral geometry to compare, align, and transfer neural representations across different spaces.

paragraphs: Learning a dynamical system involves modeling how a state changes over time, but a good fit alone does not establish stable behavior. This paper introduces Extended Linearized Contracting Dynamics, or ELCD, to give neural dynamical systems global contractivity guarantees. Contractivity concerns trajectories drawing closer under a chosen way of measuring distance, making the metric part of the guarantee.

ELCD builds its guarantees into a parameterization of the nonlinear vector field's extended linearization. In its basic form, the system is globally exponentially stable, contracts toward its equilibrium, and is globally contracting under some metric. These are properties of the construction, rather than conclusions drawn only from the observed trajectories in an experiment.

To support more general metrics in the data space, the authors learn diffeomorphisms: smooth, invertible transformations between data and latent spaces. They enforce contraction in the latent space, which ensures global contraction in the data space. Demonstrations use high-dimensional LASA, multi-link pendulum, and Rosenbrock datasets. The contribution combines learnable nonlinear dynamics with global guarantees, while using learned coordinate transformations to broaden the metrics those guarantees can accommodate.
neurips-2024-learning-neural-contracting.tldr: ELCD learns neural dynamical systems with global contraction guarantees using extended linearization and invertible transformations into a contracting latent space.

paragraphs: MaskFactory targets the demanding annotation requirements of dichotomous image segmentation, where precise masks are central to the task. Building such datasets manually takes time, money, and expertise. Synthetic data offers another route, but scene mismatches, errors caused by noise, and insufficient variety can reduce its usefulness. The paper develops a pipeline for creating diverse masks and corresponding images.

The pipeline starts by editing masks in two ways. Rigid editing uses geometric priors from diffusion models to produce precise viewpoint transformations in a zero-shot setting. Non-rigid editing combines adversarial training with self-attention to make more complex changes while maintaining topological consistency. A generation method controlled by multiple conditions then produces high-resolution images paired with accurate segmentation masks.

Experiments on DIS5K report better quality and efficiency than existing approaches. The authors also present the system as a scalable way to reduce dataset preparation time and cost. Its main design choice is to make controlled mask variation an explicit stage before producing the image-mask pairs, directly addressing both annotation precision and training-sample diversity.
neurips-2024-maskfactory-towards-high-qu.tldr: MaskFactory combines controlled mask editing with image generation to produce diverse, precise synthetic segmentation datasets.

paragraphs: MxDNA asks the model to learn how DNA should be divided into tokens. Earlier genomic foundation models commonly borrow tokenization methods from natural language, even though meaningful genomic segments can overlap, be discontinuous, or have ambiguous boundaries. The paper treats tokenization as a learnable part of the model instead of fixing that interpretation in advance.

The framework learns its strategy through gradient descent. It combines a sparse mixture of convolution experts with deformable convolution to represent the tokenization process. These components explicitly account for the unusual structure of genomic segments. This connects the choice of tokens to model training, allowing the representation of the sequence to develop alongside the model's understanding of it.

On the Nucleotide Transformer Benchmarks and Genomic Benchmarks, the authors report better performance than existing methods while using less pretraining data and time. They also show a learned tokenization strategy distinct from previous approaches and token-level capture of genomic functionality during self-supervised pretraining. These findings support adaptive tokenization for the evaluated genomic tasks; broader applications are presented as a possibility.
neurips-2024-model-decides-how-to-tokeni.tldr: MxDNA learns DNA tokenization during training, accommodating complex genomic segments and improving benchmark performance with less pretraining data and time.

paragraphs: OneBit investigates how far large language model weight compression can go while retaining useful performance. Quantization represents weights with fewer bits to reduce storage and computational overhead. Existing methods commonly use four or eight bits because pushing the precision much lower can cause severe degradation. This work targets weight matrices represented with only one bit.

The framework introduces a parameter representation designed specifically for one-bit quantization. It also uses a matrix-decomposition-based initialization method to improve convergence speed. These two components address both how the compressed weights are expressed and how training starts, rather than treating extreme compression as only a final conversion of an existing model.

The reported experiments show robust training and retention of at least 81% of non-quantized performance on the evaluated LLaMA models. That result describes retained performance in those experiments, rather than an absolute accuracy score. The contribution demonstrates that one-bit weight matrices can preserve a substantial share of model performance when paired with a tailored representation and initialization strategy.
neurips-2024-onebit-towards-extremely-lo.tldr: OneBit compresses LLM weight matrices to one bit while retaining at least 81% of non-quantized performance in the reported LLaMA experiments.

paragraphs: Best-arm identification asks an algorithm to find the option with the largest mean while keeping the probability of a wrong choice below a specified level, delta. Top-two methods repeatedly choose between the current empirical leader and its strongest challenger. A fixed probability controls that choice, but finding the probability that achieves the optimal sampling efficiency has been difficult.

The proposed algorithm replaces that fixed-probability decision with a threshold rule based on sampling allocations. When an allocation-dependent function exceeds its threshold, the algorithm samples the empirical leader; otherwise, it samples the challenger. The authors prove that this top-two-style procedure reaches the information-theoretic sample-complexity bound asymptotically as delta approaches zero.

The proof describes the long-run allocation process through fluid dynamics assembled from ordinary differential equations. Using the implicit function theorem, the authors establish existence and uniqueness of these dynamics and show that the algorithm stays close to their solution. The result resolves optimal allocation in this asymptotic regime, connecting a sequential sampling rule to a continuous description of its evolving behavior.
neurips-2024-optimal-top-two-method-for-.tldr: An allocation-based threshold rule makes top-two best-arm identification asymptotically sample-optimal as the allowed error probability approaches zero.

paragraphs: Long-term time-series forecasting can use extensive histories to improve predictions, but many approaches respond to that larger input by building increasingly large models. This paper examines whether the information in long sequences can instead be handled with a much smaller parameter set. Its proposed route is decomposition tailored to the underlying dynamics of time-series data.

The work provides both theoretical and empirical evidence that decomposition can control model growth while supporting strong forecasting. The central design principle is to exploit characteristics of the data when organizing the model, so that useful structure does not have to be captured solely through additional parameters. The proposed model uses this principle to pursue accuracy and compactness together.

Across the datasets studied, the authors report consistently superior and robust results, with over 99% fewer parameters than the majority of competing methods. The comparison concerns parameter counts and forecasting performance in those evaluations. It supports the paper's broader argument that greater model size is not invariably needed for better long-term forecasting when decomposition reflects the dynamics being modeled.
neurips-2024-parsimony-or-capability-dec.tldr: Dynamics-aware decomposition improves long-term forecasting while using over 99% fewer parameters than most competing methods in the reported comparisons.

paragraphs: Adversarial imitation learning learns behavior from expert demonstrations and has worked well with neural networks in practice. Its theoretical guarantees, however, have largely focused on simpler tabular or linear models, sometimes with algorithms that are difficult to implement. OPT-AIL aims to close that gap by studying online adversarial imitation learning with general function approximation.

The method combines online optimization of reward functions with optimism-regularized Bellman-error minimization for Q-value functions. The latter functions assess the value of actions, and their optimization incorporates the method's optimism term. Practically, the algorithm requires approximate optimization of only two objectives, making its theoretical construction more directly usable than a complex sequence of specialized procedures.

The authors prove polynomial bounds on the expert samples and environment interactions needed to learn near-expert policies. To their knowledge, this is the first provably efficient adversarial imitation learning method with general function approximation. Experiments also show better performance than previous leading deep imitation-learning methods on several challenging tasks, pairing the efficiency analysis with empirical evidence of practical effectiveness.
neurips-2024-provably-and-practically-ef.tldr: OPT-AIL combines a practical two-objective algorithm with polynomial sample and interaction guarantees for imitation learning using general function approximation.

paragraphs: RouterDC studies how to choose an appropriate language model for each incoming query from a collection of existing models. Different models have complementary abilities, so a good router can make the collection more useful than any one member. The paper focuses on a difficulty for existing routers: several models may all perform well on the same query.

The proposed router consists of an encoder and learned embeddings for the available language models. Training uses two contrastive objectives, one relating samples to models and another relating samples to samples. This dual structure makes both query-model relationships and relationships among queries part of the routing representation, addressing the ambiguity created when a query has several capable model choices.

The authors report that RouterDC outperforms individual top-performing models and existing routing approaches. Reported gains are 2.76% on in-distribution tasks and 1.90% on out-of-distribution tasks. These results support query-dependent model selection as a way to combine complementary strengths, with the dual contrastive training objective providing the paper's specific mechanism for learning that selection.
neurips-2024-routerdc-query-based-router.tldr: RouterDC learns query-to-model routing with two contrastive losses, improving the performance of assembled language models on familiar and shifted task distributions.

paragraphs: This paper develops a spiking-neural-network approach to hypergraph minimum vertex cover. Many existing spiking optimization methods first translate a problem into quadratic unconstrained binary optimization, or QUBO. Enforcing constraints in that translation can require extra slack variables. For this problem, the resulting increase in the search space can sharply reduce solver effectiveness.

The proposed architecture handles feasibility through additional spiking neurons that check constraints and apply corrections. This removes the need to express the problem through a QUBO formulation with slack-variable penalties. The correction mechanism encourages convergence toward feasible solutions, placing constraint handling directly inside the network's operation rather than expanding the binary optimization formulation.

Experiments on neuromorphic hardware produced consistently high-quality solutions on real and synthetic instances where the spiking QUBO solver often failed. The method also consumed measurably less energy than global solvers running on a CPU. These findings support direct constraint handling as a useful design choice for the evaluated problem, while the stated convergence mechanism encourages feasibility rather than guaranteeing an optimal answer on every instance.
neurips-2024-slack-free-spiking-neural-n.tldr: A spiking network checks and corrects hypergraph-cover constraints directly, avoiding slack-variable expansion and producing strong, energy-efficient experimental results.

paragraphs: Smoothed Energy Guidance, or SEG, aims to improve diffusion-model image generation without additional training or conditioning information. Classifier-free guidance has been effective for conditional generation, but extensions to unconditional models have often depended on heuristics. The paper develops guidance from an energy-based interpretation of self-attention to give the intervention a more explicit mathematical basis.

SEG defines an energy associated with self-attention and reduces the curvature of that energy landscape. It uses the resulting output as an unconditional prediction. In practice, a Gaussian kernel parameter controls the smoothing while the guidance-scale parameter stays fixed. This makes attention-energy curvature a direct control for the proposed guidance procedure.

The authors also introduce query blurring, which is equivalent to blurring the full attention weights while avoiding quadratic complexity in the number of tokens for that operation. Experiments report a Pareto improvement in generation quality and reduction of side effects: the observed improvement does not require trading one of those goals against the other. The contribution combines a guidance principle with an efficient way to implement its smoothing step.
neurips-2024-smoothed-energy-guidance-gu.tldr: SEG improves diffusion image generation without training or conditions by smoothing self-attention energy through an efficient query-blurring operation.

paragraphs: Terra is a dataset for studying environmental patterns that change across both place and time. The paper identifies limited geographic scale, short temporal coverage, and narrow reliance on time-series measurements as obstacles in existing public datasets. Terra is designed to broaden all three aspects so researchers can study environmental variation using a more extensive combination of information.

The dataset contains hourly time series for 6,480,000 grid areas worldwide across a 45-year period. It supplements those measurements with geographic images and explanatory text. This gives each research problem access to temporal observations alongside additional spatial context, making the resource multimodal rather than a collection of numerical sequences alone.

The authors provide detailed data analysis and evaluate existing deep-learning models used in earth science on the dataset. The contribution is therefore both a large data resource and an initial examination of how current methods operate on it. The stated aim is to enable stronger research in spatio-temporal data mining and environmental understanding, with more general spatio-temporal intelligence framed as a future direction.
neurips-2024-terra-a-multimodal-spatio-t.tldr: Terra combines 45 years of hourly worldwide grid data with geographic images and text for multimodal spatio-temporal research.

paragraphs: This paper seeks a better explanation for why pretraining helps models learn downstream tasks. Two properties of pretrained models have attracted attention: the flatness of the loss surface and neural collapse in learned representations. The authors investigate geometric complexity as a mechanism connecting these properties, shifting attention toward the structure of the representations themselves.

Using theory and experiments, they show that mechanisms affecting a pretrained network's geometric complexity also influence neural collapse. This links changes in representation geometry to a property used to understand pretraining's implicit biases. The work therefore treats geometric complexity as an explanatory connection between existing observations, rather than considering flatness and neural collapse independently.

The authors further show that this influence extends to neural collapse for new classes. That extension matters for transfer learning because downstream tasks involve learning beyond the original pretraining classes. The paper connects the effect to better downstream performance, particularly when only a few examples are available. Its findings contribute a geometric account of transfer behavior without presenting a complete theory of every factor behind pretraining's success.
neurips-2024-the-impact-of-geometric-com.tldr: Theory and experiments connect representation complexity to neural collapse, including for new classes, helping explain few-shot transfer performance.

paragraphs: Langevin dynamics provides a continuous-time process for sampling, but implementing it requires discrete steps. The standard Langevin Monte Carlo method can need many small steps to obtain good samples. This creates a practical cost in diffusion image generation, where reducing the number of steps can quickly reduce image quality.

The Poisson Midpoint Method approximates small-step Langevin Monte Carlo using larger steps. It modifies a randomized midpoint approach previously developed for strongly log-concave distributions. The motivating applications include distributions without that shape restriction and dynamics whose drift changes over time. The authors prove that their method can obtain a quadratic speedup over Langevin Monte Carlo under assumptions they describe as very weak.

In image-generation experiments, the method maintains the quality of a DDPM requiring 1,000 neural-network calls using only 50–80 calls. It also outperforms ODE-based approaches at similar compute in those experiments. The contribution combines a discretization-efficiency result with evidence that the larger-step approximation can preserve sample quality in a demanding generative-model setting.
neurips-2024-the-poisson-midpoint-method.tldr: Poisson Midpoint approximates fine-step Langevin sampling with larger steps, achieving a conditional quadratic speedup and strong diffusion-generation results.

paragraphs: Training-data attribution estimates how a model's behavior would change if particular training examples were removed. Efficient methods based on implicit differentiation can miss the effects of the optimization algorithm, multiple possible fitted solutions, or training pipelines with several stages. Methods that unroll the training process address these issues, but become difficult to scale.

Source connects these two approaches through approximate unrolling. It accounts for the training process using an approximation that can be evaluated with a formula resembling an influence function. The goal is to retain useful information about how training produced the model while avoiding the computational burden of directly unrolling that process.

The authors describe Source as suitable for cases that challenge implicit-differentiation methods, including models that have not converged and pipelines with multiple training stages. Experiments show better counterfactual prediction than existing attribution methods, especially in those difficult settings. These findings support incorporating training history into attribution efficiently: the relevant question is how removing data would affect the trained model through its learning procedure.
neurips-2024-training-data-attribution-v.tldr: Source uses approximate training unrolling to estimate data-removal effects efficiently, improving attribution for non-converged models and multistage training.

paragraphs: This paper examines how several transformer components learn to work together for in-context learning. Its setting is a transformer with two attention layers trained on n-gram Markov-chain data, where each token statistically depends on the previous n tokens. The analysis includes relative positional embeddings, multi-head softmax attention, and a normalized feed-forward layer.

The authors prove that gradient flow for a cross-entropy in-context-learning objective converges to a limiting model implementing a generalized induction-head mechanism with a learned feature. Each component has a distinct role. The first attention layer copies tokens from a past window to each position. The feed-forward network and normalization select informationally relevant parents from that window to form a feature vector.

The second attention layer compares those features with the feature at the output position and uses the similarities to generate the output. Simulations further validate the theory. The result explains how copying, feature selection, and classification emerge together in the studied architecture and data setting, extending the theoretical account beyond the contribution of attention alone.
neurips-2024-unveiling-induction-heads-p.tldr: For a two-attention-layer transformer on Markov-chain data, the authors prove that training yields coordinated copying, feature selection, and induction-style prediction.
